effort_detection.where: ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (SQLite, read from a copy): OpenCode 2.x table session_v2 has model {id, providerID, variant}, version and token counts; session_message rows of type assistant carry data.model with the variant. Older 1.x sessions: tables session/message (message.data.modelID, variant). Also `opencode session export <id>`. The --format json events carry no variant. A session without a variant records none.

logs.where: ~/.t3/userdata/logs/provider/events.<thread>.log: the model and effort it opened each provider session with (claudeAgent query.open options.model / options.effort; cursor run.start options.model {id, params: reasoning_effort / reasoning / effort, fast}) and turn usage. Several threads can share one file: filter by the threadId in each line. The harness's own record (Claude Code session file, OpenCode DB, Cursor SDK store, Antigravity conversation DB) comes first; this log is the fallback.

launchers.notes: An app that starts harness sessions, not a harness: it runs Claude through the Claude Agent SDK (Claude Code's harness), Codex through the Codex App Server, and the other engines through their own SDKs or CLIs (https://x.com/theo/status/2113424203345265053). A seat started in it ranks as the harness it ran (declare t3-code:<harness>, e.g. t3-code:claude-code); the launcher is recorded in the seat's details, never as a leaderboard row. T3 Code gives every session its own MCP server and adds instructions to it, which the seat details show.
